verdicts.reason: User at CLIENT01 starts the connection. rdp01.1sn0s.lab is labelled on the target rack. Caption 'Secure RDP connection'. No private keys exist yet.
An amber pulse runs along the floor channel from the client to the rdp01 rack. Nothing is green. No keys exist yet.
The pulse arrives at rdp01 and the listener lights. The server, not the client, is the holder. Caption correct. No keys exist yet.

A pale card tagged 'Self-signed' travels to the client, which shows 'Unverified'. The channel stays amber, and the amber dies out of the channel by tile 6 (attempt closed). The self-seal itself is too small to resolve at 960x540, but the tag states it. No CA-issued key exists yet.
The RDPAuth badge drops from above the AD node onto the rdp01 rack. No connection is pending; the channel is dark. No certificate or key comes from AD.

The key pair forms inside the opened RDP01 chassis: a private key with a padlock-body head and a hollow-ring public key. Caption 'The private key stays on the server'. RDP private key: formed inside the chassis beside its open container (tiles 3-6, frame c).

The padlock-headed private key drops into the box container (tile 2), the lid closes (tiles 3-4), and the dial lock shows (tiles 5-6, frame c). The public key stays outside. RDP private key: inside its locked container from tile 3 to the end.

The ring public key enters the glass capsule at the octagon port plate (tiles 1-2). Caption 'The request is signed, not the key sent'. The small white loop at the capsule's left end is the port plate's ring fixture: the identical fixture is on WEB01's port before any web capsule exists (B-07.2_b_f2235.png), it never travels, and it has no shaft or padlock body. RDP private key: inside its locked container (closed box with dial) in every frame and tile.

A straight light beam from the container's lid seals the capsule (tiles 2-3, frame b), and the capsule gains a seal band. No key-shaped object moves. RDP private key: inside its locked container in all frames and tiles. The container glows but stays shut.

The capsule is held just outside the RDP01 chassis at its port side, framed with the 1SN0S.LAB AD pillar, and does not enter AD. A route lights toward Issuing CA 1 only (cyan floor line, frame c). The separate steel-blue query pulse is not visible in the samples (MINOR). RDP private key: inside its closed container, visible lower-left in the open chassis in all frames and tiles. Only the port ring fixture stays at the port.

A bare capsule travels the lit cyan route into Issuing CA 1. It never goes near the root or CA 2, and nothing is attached to it in any tile. RDP private key: inside its locked container in the RDP01 chassis (tiles 1-3, frame a). CA1 key: inside the sealed cyan module (frame c, tiles 4-6).

Four staggered ticks appear inside Issuing CA 1, but check 1, 'Requester authenticated', is hidden behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label in frames b and c and in tiles 2-6. The hovering capsule also covers 'Enroll permission'. In practice the viewer reads three checks, so F-06 step 1 is lost. The caption is correct. RDP private key: off-screen, last seen locked in its container; nothing key-like left the server. CA1 key: in its sealed module (left block) in all frames.

The capsule is consumed at the press (tiles 1-3). A drive rod from the sealed module drives the press, which stamps a card labelled 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab' and 'Remote Desktop Authentication' (frames b and c). After stamping, a white ring glyph stays under the press head. I identify it as the press's issuer-seal die: it has no shaft or padlock body and is fixed to the press head. A validity bar and the AIA/CDP ports cannot be resolved at this tier (MINOR). CA1 key: inside the sealed cyan module in every tile. RDP private key: off-screen, last seen locked in its container.

The card returns along the cyan route and locks in beside the closed dial container in the RDP01 chassis (frame c, tiles 5-6). A separate translucent intermediate copy cannot be told apart from the server card at this tier (MINOR), but B-06.1 later shows the server presenting two cards. The CA1 crown card stays in place. RDP private key: inside its locked container next to the new card (frame c, tiles 5-6). The container never opened. CA1 key: in its module.

The camera cranes to the gold 1SN0S Root CA vault on a cable-free plinth. The ring seal is shown as an existing property. The root's press and the dark module cube are still and dark. RDP private key: inside its locked container beside the card (frame a, tile 1). CA1 key: in its module. Root key: inside its dark module cube on the plinth.

A desaturated flashback marked 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony'. The capsule tagged 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' leaves CA1 (tile 2) on removable media and reaches the root plinth (frame b), where the press issues the CA certificate (tile 4), which is carried back (tile 5). The caption wording is correct. The CA=true band and the sealing by CA1's module cannot be resolved (MINOR). The present-day RDP check list is still visible inside CA1 during the flashback (MINOR anachronism). Root key: in its module cube. CA1 key: in its module. RDP private key: not in the flashback.

Back in the present, a link grows from the CA1 crown card to the root seal. The root stays cable-free. Caption 'The Root CA is the trust anchor'. No request travels. The link renders near-white rather than gold-to-cyan (MINOR, C-10). Root, CA1 and RDP private keys: in their module or container (RDP chassis visible bottom centre, frame c).

A new amber pulse reaches the server (tile 2, frame b). Then two cyan cards (the server certificate and CA1 copy) travel to the client (tile 3, frame c). No handshake proof (signature impression), key pulse or proof-verification moment can be seen in any frame or tile, so the shot reads as the certificates alone authenticating the server (F-10). RDP private key: inside its container in the open chassis (frame b). No key-shaped object travels with the cards. CA keys: in their modules.

The cards dock upward: server certificate, Issuing CA 1, then the gold root already in its cradle, which was visible since B-02.2. 'Installed earlier by policy' shimmer. Nothing travels from AD. Caption correct. RDP private key: off-screen in its locked container; no key is near the client.
A small AIA indicator with 'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it' and 'Fetching never creates trust'. Nothing is fetched. RDP private key: off-screen in its locked container.

Six distinct staggered checks. Checks 1-5 resolve, including 'Name matches rdp01.1sn0s.lab' and 'EKU permits RDP'. 'Revocation OK' appears with an amber pending tick (frame c, tile 6). RDP private key: off-screen in its locked container.

Two amber CRL fetches leave the pki.1sn0s.lab kiosk (tiles 2-3), and two scrolls land, one beside the server card and one beside the CA1 card (frame c). None goes to the root. 'OCSP if deployed' sits on the client's check list, and the revocation tick then turns green. RDP private key: inside its container in the RDP01 chassis (frame b, lower right; tile 4).

The channel turns from amber to green only after all six ticks, and the session window opens. Caption correct. The caption already fades in at the end of B-06.5 while the channel is still amber (MINOR). RDP private key: off-screen in its container.

The camera glides to WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab, with a WebServer-TLS badge behind its label. RDP private key: inside its locked dial container beside the installed card in the open RDP01 chassis (frame a). Web key not formed yet.

A web key pair forms inside WEB01 (tile 2). The padlock-headed private key drops into the box (tile 3), the lid closes, the ring public key enters the capsule (tile 4), and a beam from the container seals it (tile 5). WEB01's port ring fixture is already present before the capsule (frame b), which identifies the same fixture on RDP01. WEB private key: inside its locked container from tile 4 onward. RDP private key: off-screen, last seen locked.

A query diamond from AD (frame b). CA1 is tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here'. CA2 shows 'Template published / Enrollment policy / Permissions / CA available' and a violet route. The capsule stays at WEB01's port. CA1 is only partly dimmed, not clearly muted grey (MINOR). WEB private key: inside its locked container (frame a; tiles 1-3). RDP private key: in its container in the RDP01 chassis (frame c, lower left).

A bare capsule travels only along the violet route into Issuing CA 2. It goes nowhere near CA1 or the root. WEB private key: inside its locked container in WEB01 (frame b, tiles 3-4). CA2 key: in its sealed violet module (frame c). RDP private key: in its container (frame a, lower left).

Compressed checks run inside CA2. 'Requester authenticated' is hidden behind the CA label, and the required note 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is printed on top of 'Request meets template policy', so both are illegible (frames b and c, tiles 4-6). The F-07 restriction is not conveyed. CA2 key: inside its sealed module. WEB private key: off-screen, locked.

The capsule is consumed. CA2's press stamps a card labelled 'portal.1sn0s.lab' and 'Server Authentication' (frame b), which returns to WEB01 and locks beside the closed container (tile 5). Caption correct. A separate CA2 intermediate copy cannot be resolved (MINOR). WEB private key: inside its locked container beside the card (tile 5). The port ring fixture stays at the plate (frame c). CA2 key: in its module.

The existing CA2 crown card is linked to the same root seal. The root's press and module cube stay dark and still. The link renders near-white rather than gold (MINOR, C-10). All keys are in their modules or containers: root cube on the plinth, CA modules, and the RDP01 and WEB01 chassis (frame c).

An amber pulse reaches WEB01. The violet cards travel to the client and dock: portal certificate, CA2, then the gold root. Compressed ticks 'Name matches portal.1sn0s.lab / EKU permits TLS server auth / Currently valid / Revocation OK', and the channel turns green. The proof and the per-link CRL fetches are not resolvable in the samples (MINOR). WEB and RDP private keys: off-screen or in their chassis containers; nothing key-like travels with the cards.

Hero topology: the root on top, CA1 and CA2 below, RDP01 under CA1, WEB01 under CA2. Cyan and violet paths rise and converge at the single cable-free root. Caption correct. The convergence renders white, not gold, and the user is outside the hero framing (MINOR). Root module and press stay dark. All keys are in their modules or containers.

Title card 'Certificate Flow — From request to trust' over the topology, then a fade to black (the black final frame is the intended end of the fade). All keys remain in their modules or containers until the fade.

findings.evidence: Only the two cyan certificate cards are seen travelling from RDP01 to the client (tile 3, frame c). No key pulse inside the closed container, no signature-impression handshake proof and no impression matching or dissolving at the client is discernible in any frame or tile.
findings.why: Without a visible proof of possession, the presentation reads as 'sending the certificate authenticates the server'. F-10 says a certificate alone proves nothing.
findings.direction: Make the in-container key pulse and the handshake-proof impression (with its match and dissolve at the client) clearly visible and large enough to read at the animatic tier, travelling after the cards and separate from them.

findings.evidence: The '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' name label sits on top of check 1 'Requester authenticated' for the whole beat. The hovering capsule covers part of 'Enroll permission granted'.
findings.why: The viewer sees three checks. Requester authentication, the first CA check in F-06, is never legible.
findings.direction: Keep all four check rows clear of the CA name label and the capsule while they resolve.

findings.evidence: 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is rendered on top of 'Request meets template policy', so both are unreadable. 'Requester authenticated' is again hidden behind the CA2 label.
findings.why: The F-07 point that the subject comes from the request, which is why Enroll is restricted, is not conveyed, and check 1 is lost again.
findings.direction: Give the restriction note its own unobstructed line and keep the check rows clear of the CA label.

findings.evidence: The route to CA1 lights, but no separate steel-blue query pulse to AD and back can be seen in any sample. In B-07.3 the diamond pulse is visible.
findings.why: Without the visible lookup, the route choice looks arbitrary rather than discovered from the Enrollment Services objects (F-05).
findings.direction: Show the steel-blue query pulse travelling to AD and back before the route lights.

findings.evidence: The trust links from the CA crowns to the root seal render near-white instead of gold-to-cyan and gold-to-violet.
findings.why: The links lose the colour language that ties both paths to the single gold root.
findings.direction: Use the role tokens on the trust links.

findings.evidence: The CA=true band on the CA request and its sealing by CA1's own module cannot be resolved. The present-day RDP check list ('Template published on this CA'…) stays visible inside CA1 during the flashback.
findings.why: The flashback should be visibly separate from the RDP enrollment. Present-tense check results in a setup-era scene blur that separation.
findings.direction: Make the band and the module sealing legible, and hide the present-tense check list during the flashback.

findings.evidence: Only one returning card can be told apart. The translucent intermediate copy travelling with it and settling into a separate intermediate store is not distinguishable (the same applies in B-08.2).
findings.why: B-06.1 presents an intermediate copy whose arrival was not clearly shown.
findings.direction: Make the translucent copy visibly distinct and give it its own slot in the chassis.

findings.evidence: The caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' is already fading in during B-06.5 while the channel is still amber.
findings.why: The trust claim slightly precedes the green channel.
findings.direction: Start the caption only once the channel has turned green.
